ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides who fixes round 5 and how the re-review runs.

ACTION: Dispatch the round-5 fix implementer with model `opus` at the highest effort the dispatch accepts. It starts fresh unless `fix-loop.md` says otherwise. The prompt is the Task 6 brief from `scripts/task-brief`, plus F1 verbatim. It orders the work as reproduce, fix, then verify, and it carries no history of rounds 1 to 4.

Task 6 is not done. The scoped re-review still reports F1 (the Important finding that the invalidation races with the background refresh at `cache/refresh.py:88`). The new test passes only because it never starts the refresh thread, so it proves nothing about the race.

This is fix attempt 5 of 5. I am sending it to an opus implementer at the highest effort the dispatch accepts. I am not switching to another model. Round 4 already ran on opus at high effort with full context, but it never reproduced the race. A fix without a reproduction is a guess, so the missing piece is the reproduction and not model strength.

The brief for this round sets three steps in a fixed order:
1. Write a test that starts the refresh thread and fails on the current code. Show the failing output.
2. Fix the race until that test passes. Repeat the test many times to show it is stable.
3. Run the covering tests and report their output.

When the report arrives, I generate a new review package and dispatch a scoped re-review. If F1 is still open after this round, the cap is reached. I then stop and adjudicate as `fix-loop.md` says, and I bring you the evidence. If F1 is closed, I record Task 6 in the ledger and continue with the next task.
